key_insight: An open gain-cell/eDRAM library with measured retention lowers the entry cost for U.S. teams. It is useful test infrastructure for the gain-cell ideas, not a bit-supply lever.
killer_doubt: A 130 nm cell is ~1-3 um2, >1,000x the 864 nm2 1b cell. The 22FDX PDK is NDA-bound, so it cannot be published. OpenGCRAM already exists.
decisive_experiment: Not worth funding standalone. If wanted, put a 64 kb SKY130/GF180 gain-cell macro with on-die retention BIST on a free or ~$10k open shuttle and contribute the data to OpenGCRAM.
prior_art: OpenGCRAM (Stanford/Wong group, arXiv 2507.10849, 2025, built on OpenRAM) (via search snippet); OpenRAM (UCSC/OSU); open SKY130/GF180 shuttles.

key_insight: A CIS pinned node is the lowest-leakage storage node in silicon (~1-10 e-/s). Its hot-pixel statistics are a ready analogue of the DRAM retention tail.
killer_doubt: At 0.5-1 um2 the cell is ~600-1,200x the 1b cell. Dark current rises ~100-1,000x from 25 to 85 C. IGZO 2T0C gives >1,000 s retention in far less area.
decisive_experiment: Only as a test vehicle: on one CIS MPW (~$150k), map dark-current tails of 1e6 pinned storage nodes at 25-85 C, at 1.1 um and the smallest pitch allowed, to calibrate Jot-RAM (N-84) scaling.
prior_art: Global-shutter in-pixel storage nodes (Sony, Samsung, OmniVision); Jot-RAM N-84 in triage; IGZO/ZTO 2T0C gain cells (imec, N-26) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Planar pseudocapacitance in principle gives ~4-5 fF on a 30 nm pad with no HAR etch. That would be the ideal answer to the capacitor wall.
killer_doubt: Faradaic redox endures ~1e5-1e6 cycles against the 1e13-1e15 needed. Pseudocapacitor knee frequencies are Hz-kHz, not the ~100 MHz a ns write needs. Hydrous RuO2 needs water in BEOL.
decisive_experiment: A ~$80k coupon test: ALD RuO2 or MXene on a Nafion-class or solid-acid film, 1 um2 pads, 10 ns pulses at 85 C. Kill if <50% of the charge moves in 10 ns or it fails before 1e9 cycles.
prior_art: Triage N-25 (pseudocapacitive variant dead on faradaic endurance) and N-17 (ZettaCore molecular redox memory); Gogotsi MXene micro-supercapacitors [training knowledge].

key_insight: Reusing the donor crystal while stacking single-crystal membranes attacks epi cost. Smart-Cut donor reuse already captures most of that value.
killer_doubt: Remote epitaxy is shown for polar crystals, not Si. 64 bond and imprint steps make cost linear in tiers (0.99^64 = 53% yield). Floating-body retention failed at Z-RAM.
decisive_experiment: A ~$300k test: grow Si through monolayer graphene on Si(001), peel it, and check XRD rocking width and DLTS defect density. Then measure floating-body retention at 85 C on 10 transferred films. Kill if >1e9 cm-2 dislocations or <64 ms.
prior_art: MIT Jeehwan Kim remote epitaxy (polar: GaAs, GaN, LiF); Soitec Smart-Cut donor reuse; NEO 3D X-DRAM and Unisantis DFM floating-body; Innovative Silicon Z-RAM [training knowledge].

key_insight: A compiler TTL tag per page is the right software contract for a retention-class tier. It is folded into I-01854, which pairs it with a cell change.
killer_doubt: A 100 ms worst case is today's 64 ms cell, so no capacitor saving follows. KV pages live seconds, not 50 ms. RANA, ZEM and N-64 already skip refresh.
decisive_experiment: Covered by I-01854's trace study. Standalone, disable refresh on one DDR5 FPGA channel and run LLM decode with TTL eviction. Measure bit errors against the refresh-on baseline (~$50k).
prior_art: RANA (Tsinghua, ISCA 2018); ZEM (IEEE Access 2021); CAMEL eDRAM co-design (2023) (via search snippet); Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); triage N-64.

key_insight: A permanent 2x-refresh code in MR4 lets stock controllers absorb weak-tail dies with zero capex, much like B4-03's relaxed-retention HBM bin.
killer_doubt: After row/column repair and DDR5 on-die ECC, retention-only fallout is likely <1-3% of dies. Makers already sell such dies through temperature grades, downbins and UTT channels in a shortage.
decisive_experiment: A ~$100k test: buy 1,000 UTT/downbin DDR5 dies and screen their retention at 85 C with 32 and 16 ms refresh. Kill if <50% pass at 2x refresh or if the recoverable volume is <1% of supply.
prior_art: Industry downbinning, extended-temperature 2x refresh grades and UTT/eTT die sales; RAIDR multi-rate refresh (CMU 2012); triage N-64/B4-03 retention bin [training knowledge].

key_insight: Area-cost arbitrage is real: processed DRAM silicon costs ~$100k/m2 against display-class backplanes at ~$100-300/m2. Oxide 1T1C works with no silicon crystal.
killer_doubt: Web overlay is microns against ~15 nm needed (20 ppm/K foil: 20 um/K per metre). At realistic >=$1-5k/m2 and 17x lower density, the gain is <=1-6x, not 100x.
decisive_experiment: A ~$400k sheet-level test: one self-aligned multilevel imprint stamp defines a 4 kb IGZO 1T1C array at 100 nm on steel foil. Kill if functional cells are <99.9% or overlay error is >30 nm.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll self-aligned imprint (2000s); U. Michigan roll-to-roll nanoimprint (Guo); PragmatIC FlexIC; Thinfilm printed memory; Holst Centre flexible IGZO [training knowledge].

key_insight: Strain-driven rolling multiplies the area per footprint by ~pi x N. That is a volume-density trick, worth something only where footprint is the constraint.
killer_doubt: Rolling folds already-patterned area. Cost scales with patterned area (~63x footprint for 20 windings), so cost per bit stays planar. Contacting 20 windings needs a staircase.
decisive_experiment: A ~$150k test: roll a 5-winding IGZO TFT membrane, then measure winding-to-winding contact yield and TFT shift after rolling. Model the cost per patterned area first. It decides the idea before any fabrication.
prior_art: Rolled-up nanotechnology (O. G. Schmidt, IFW Dresden/TU Chemnitz): rolled-up capacitors, batteries and TFTs [training knowledge].

key_insight: The 3D XPoint deck architecture plus a capacitor could give a transistor-less stacked 4F2 DRAM on idle chalcogenide tools. The selector, not the deck, is the problem.
killer_doubt: Hold leakage must be <=3-16 fA (1-5 fF, 0.2 V, 64 ms); an OTS at ~V/2 leaks pA-nA, a 1e3-1e5x gap. OTS endurance (~1e9-1e11) misses 1e13+ hot-row writes.
decisive_experiment: A ~$60k test: measure the I-V floor of 100 OTS devices (20-40 nm) at 0.2-0.6 V and 85 C with an electrometer, then cycle to 1e11 with a 1 fF series capacitor. Kill if leakage >1 pA.
prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint OTS; SK hynix/Micron selector-only memory; triage N-85 crested-barrier 1S1C (the better selector route) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Each access transistor as the current source for its own node gives self-alignment and a built-in yield screen. Idsat sets the plating rate, so the spread is ~5-10%.
killer_doubt: Moldless plating is isotropic: domes merge at ~half pitch (~20 nm), so AR 100 is impossible. Drivers must be powered in electrolyte. Selective electroless already seeds on pads.
decisive_experiment: A ~$120k test: on a test array of 1k transistors at 1 um pitch with a TEOS hole mold, plate through the transistors, then measure height spread against Idsat. Separately confirm that domes merge on unmolded pads.
prior_art: Template electrodeposition in AAO (Masuda 1995); bottom-up Co/Ru superfill and selective electroless caps (Intel, IBM); triage N-21 AAO mold and N-82 plated holes [training knowledge].

key_insight: Once N-04 sensing fixes the signal, retention binds. ~1 fF with a Si access device gives ~27 ms, matching HBM's 18-29 ms full sweep: access becomes refresh, pillar ~5x shorter.
killer_doubt: Planar 0.5 fF needs ~7,000 nm2 (8x the cell), so a ~240 nm stub is needed. At 95 C the tail halves to ~13 ms, below sweep; +25 ns tRCD.
decisive_experiment: (1) Profile lifetime and access-period histograms from production LLM inference and training traces (~$50k). (2) On FPGA DDR5/HBM, cut refresh 4x and run decode with access-certified rows, counting errors at 85-95 C. Pair with N-04's 1 fF MPW.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018), ZEM (2021), CAMEL eDRAM co-design (2023) (via search snippet); triage N-64 lease and N-04 sensing. No capacitor-shrink co-design found (search summary).

key_insight: With an IGZO node (~1 aA), transfer-path noise, not leakage, limits the electron count. A capacitor-free 1T node at ~200-300 e- on short bitlines would be 3D-ready.
killer_doubt: Frozen kTC on a 35 fF bitline is ~82 e- rms; 50 e- at 8 sigma needs a <=0.06 fF path (CCD or in-cell gain). Skipper cannot average pre-transfer noise.
decisive_experiment: A ~$400k test: a BEOL-IGZO MPW array with 0.02-0.1 fF 1T nodes on 8-, 16- and 64-cell bitlines, read by charge-transfer pre-sense plus CDS. Measure BER against electrons per bit (50-1,000) and the 85 C retention tail.
prior_art: Hitachi PLEDM few-electron gain cell (1990s); Fermilab skipper CCD (Tiffenberg 2017); Fossum/Gigajot QIS jots; triage N-04, N-84, N-08 [training knowledge].
